source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Press load default,save and reboot.
3. Boot in BIOS,compare setting should matches SPEC.
4. Change BIOS all/random setting in this function,to non-default  setting.
5. Save and reboot.
6. Boot in BIOS and check your setting still exist.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The default setting should matches SPEC."
2. No error log happen.
3. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
4. Check your set still exist.

original_test_intent: Verify ACPI defaults against SPEC first, then verify that approved non-default firmware controls persist without corrupting ACPI table exposure, device/interrupt topology, power-state behavior, thermal safeguards, OS boot or management recovery.
original_method: Manually Load Default and compare named ACPI fields with SPEC, then set a bounded non-default matrix, save/reboot or cold boot as documented, visually verify persistence and correlate the OS-visible ACPI/device/power/thermal state.
manual_activity: An engineer must interpret and operate the ACPI firmware page, load defaults, apply approved changes, execute any required cold boot and visually accept values. Automated ACPI table and OS checks only corroborate effects.
required_inputs: Board/BIOS/BMC and approved test OS identity
Exact ACPI fields and their table/device/interrupt/power/thermal effects
SPEC defaults and safe non-default values
Expected ACPI table signatures/revisions and OS enumeration
Required warm reset versus cold boot plus console/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or disable thermal/protection behavior without explicit bounded approval.
Do not infer ACPI safety across different BIOS, OS kernel or hardware populations.
Capture device/interrupt/power/thermal baselines and keep an independent console.
Stop on boot failure, missing/duplicated device, interrupt storm, sleep/resume fault, thermal/power anomaly or management loss.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only ACPI table inventory/checksum metadata, OS device/interrupt topology, power/thermal state, kernel logs and BMC health.
Compare approved effects across default and non-default operator phases.
Do not drive BIOS, trigger unsafe power states or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve fields/defaults, expected ACPI consequences, reset type and recovery.
Perform/capture default-first and non-default firmware phases.
Evaluate firmware plus OS/hardware evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects BIOS automation. No source command exists; OS ACPI utilities cannot prove the displayed firmware values and are supporting evidence only.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the firmware procedure and use platform-approved read-only ACPI/table/device collection with versions recorded. Do not replace it with OS power-policy changes.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The default-first sequence, null script and 5/20-minute fields are retained; all/random remains source text only.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each firmware field to affected ACPI objects and expected OS-visible topology or power/thermal behavior; capture tables and health at baseline, defaults, persistence and final restoration using the required reset type.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact board/BIOS/ACPI implementation, hardware population and approved OS/kernel.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, OS/kernel, ACPI compiler/parser and inventory-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform ACPI field documentation, supported OS guidance and ACPI specification revision implemented by the firmware.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces arbitrary changes with a field/artifact/behavior matrix and reset semantics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; preserves defaults/persistence and adds table, topology and protection evidence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Field map, expected artifacts, reset type, defaults and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Table differences can be legitimate and require platform-aware comparison; raw byte diffs alone are not a verdict.

project_override_considerations: The project may approve a subset of ACPI controls and OS states. Completion applies only to that field/OS/hardware matrix and cannot claim untested sleep, hot-plug, NUMA or thermal behavior.
expected_evidence: Platform/OS identity, field-effect matrix, approval and recovery
Baseline ACPI tables, device/interrupt topology, power/thermal and boot health
Load Default captures and SPEC/table/health comparison
Non-default captures, persistence and expected artifact/behavior deltas
Final state, logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The default-first then non-default persistence lifecycle matches the criteria. Missing values/effects are project readiness information, not conflicting source facts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The ACPI lifecycle intent is clear. Exact field mapping, reset type and recovery are necessary gates but do not permanently block the case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees on manual operation and adds ACPI-specific artifact and safety analysis.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its ACPI/OS evidence improvements but corrects classification to MANUAL ONLY.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Preserves default-first ordering, bounds random changes and separates firmware acceptance from OS-visible consequence collection.

review_improvement: Connects each ACPI field to concrete firmware tables and OS/hardware behavior while explicitly protecting thermal, power and interrupt safety.
independent_technical_reasoning: Core configuration and visual acceptance occur in pre-OS firmware. Automated ACPI and OS evidence begins after those human actions and cannot replace them, so MANUAL ONLY applies.
no_automatic_retry: Do not automatically repeat ACPI changes, cold boot, sleep/resume or reboot after device/power/thermal anomalies; preserve first evidence and obtain engineer disposition.
